title: Nabeel S. Qureshi | Substack
text:
Nabeel S. Qureshi | Substack
I can’t speak to specific details here, but Palantir software is partly responsible for stopping multiple terror attacks. I believe this fact alone vindicates this stance. [...] Palantir was an unusually intense and weird place. I remember my first time I talked to Stephen Cohen) he had the A/C in his office set at 60, several weird-looking devices for minimizing CO2 content in the room, and had a giant pile of ice in a cup. Throughout the conversation, he kept chewing pieces of ice. (Apparently there are cognitive benefits to this.) [...] One side note: the company was often cast as a ‘data company’ in the press, or worse, a ‘data mining’ company or similar. As far as I can tell, this was a simple misunderstanding on the press’s part. Palantir does data integration for companies, but the data is owned by the companies – not Palantir. “Mining” data usually means using somebody else’s data for your own profits, or selling it. Palantir doesn’t do that - customer data stays with the customer.
